text: Is not the life of a mortal on earth a hard service? Are not his days like the days of a hired laborer?
Like a slave longing for the shade, like a hired hand waiting for his wages,
so I have been allotted months of emptiness, and nights of misery have been assigned to me.
When I lie down I ask, "When will I get up?" But the night drags on, and I am filled with tossing until dawn.
My flesh is clothed with worms and clods of dust; my skin scabs over and oozes.
My days pass more swiftly than a weaver's shuttle, and they come to an end without hope.
Remember that my life is but a breath; my eye will never again see anything good.
The eye that now sees me will see me no more; your eyes will turn toward me, but I will be gone.

versions.text: The eye that now sees me will see me no more; your eyes will look for me, and I will be gone.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew is "your eyes are upon me, and I am not." "Look for me" suggests searching, which anticipates verse 21 rather than rendering this line; "turn toward me" keeps the sense of God's gaze falling on one who has vanished.

text: As a cloud fades and vanishes, so the one who goes down to the grave does not come up again.
He never returns to his house; his place knows him no more.
So I, for my part, will not restrain my mouth; I will speak in the anguish of my spirit, I will complain in the bitterness of my soul.

versions.text: Therefore I will not keep silent. I will speak out of the anguish of my spirit; I will complain in the bitterness of my soul.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew גַּם־אֲנִי emphasizes "I too / I for my part," and לֹא אֶחֱשָׂךְ פִּי is literally "I will not hold back my mouth." The emphatic pronoun is lost in the current rendering.

versions.text: So I, for my part, will not restrain my mouth.
versions.explanation: Two full clauses of the Hebrew were dropped: אֲדַבְּרָה בְּצַר רוּחִי ("I will speak in the distress of my spirit") and אָשִׂיחָה בְּמַר נַפְשִׁי ("I will complain in the bitterness of my soul"). The emphatic "I, for my part" from the earlier revision is retained, and the missing parallel lines are restored.

text: Am I the sea, or a sea monster, that you set a guard over me?
When I think my bed will comfort me and my couch will ease my complaint,
then you terrify me with dreams and horrify me with visions,
so that I would choose strangling and death rather than this body of mine.
I despise my life; I would not live forever. Leave me alone, for my days are a breath.
What is a mortal, that you make so much of him, that you set your heart upon him,
that you examine him every morning and test him every moment?
Will you never look away from me, or let me alone long enough to swallow my spit?
If I have sinned, what can I do to you, you watcher of mankind? Why have you made me your target, so that I have become a burden to myself?

versions.text: If I have sinned, what have I done to you, you watcher of mankind? Why have you made me your target? Have I become a burden to you?
versions.explanation: The Hebrew text reads עָלַי ("to myself"), not "to you." The rendering "a burden to you" follows an ancient scribal tradition rather than the received text, and turning the clause into a separate question obscures its connection to the preceding line. A footnote could note the ancient tradition that read "a burden to you."

versions.text: If I have sinned, what have I done to you, you watcher of mankind? Why have you made me your target, so that I have become a burden to myself?
versions.explanation: אֶפְעַל is an imperfect verb, so the sense is present/future — "what do I do to you?" or "what can I do to you?" — i.e. how can my sin possibly harm you? The past-tense "what have I done to you" shifts the argument from the powerlessness of Job's sin to affect God toward a simple protest of innocence. A footnote could still be added noting that an ancient scribal tradition read "a burden to you" at the end of the verse.

text: Why do you not pardon my offense and take away my guilt? For soon I will lie down in the dust; you will search for me, and I will be no more.
